title: 6. Who or What Forces the Protagonist to Confront Themselves?
use_cases: Use when evaluating if supporting characters are driving the protagonist's growth.
Implement when mapping out the internal and external obstacles of a screenplay.
Configure when designing a character biography to ensure multi-dimensional traits.
Use when diagnosing why a script's narrative energy or stakes feel stagnant.
content:
Every great script features catalysts that kick the protagonist out of complacency. Sometimes it’s a worthy antagonist, a relentless mentor, or a life event that raises the stakes.

Greenlight Coverage has seen, time after time, that mentor or rival dynamics can elevate a script from functional to unforgettable. We highlight these in our coverage, pinpointing who, what, and how your story tests your lead.

Key Catalysts and Their Story Impact

- Life-altering event: Forces immediate confrontation with uncomfortable truths.
- Mirroring character: Reveals flaws and blind spots by analogy, leading to self-awareness.
- Mentor: Offers new perspectives but holds the protagonist accountable for change, as with Yoda and Luke Skywalker.
- Antagonist: Blocks progress, challenges assumptions, raises personal stakes.

We nudge you to scrutinize every character and event circling your protagonist. Are they active agents of change, or passive background? The right catalyst propels your hero forward—and your story with it.

Develop Rich Characters with This Guided Biography Worksheet

It’s easy to focus on plot and overlook character.

This worksheet helps you map the details that bring them to life.

See What’s Inside

Obstacles power your story. Without constant friction, your protagonist never earns their arc—and your script loses energy fast. You need a sharp mix of inner demons and relentless outside pressure.
